The '''nine windows''' technique, also known as '''9 windows''', '''9 boxes''', '''9 screens''', '''multiscreen diagram''', or '''system operator tool''' is a [[creative problem-solving]] [[Creativity_techniques#In_problem_solving|technique]] that analyzes a problem across time and relative to its place within a [[Systems engineering|system]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Chakrabarti |first1=Amaresh |last2=Blessing |first2=Lucienne T. M. |title=An Anthology of Theories and Models of Design: Philosophy, Approaches and Empirical Explorations |date=13 February 2014 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-1-4471-6338-1 |pages=254 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=R_O8BAAAQBAJ&dq=Nine+windows+multiscreen&pg=PA254 |access-date=3 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Chechurin |first1=Leonid |title=Research and Practice on the Theory of Inventive Problem Solving (TRIZ): Linking Creativity, Engineering and Innovation |date=12 September 2016 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-319-31782-3 |pages=269 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RzIPDQAAQBAJ&dq=Nine+windows+multiscreen&pg=PA269 |access-date=3 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Gupta |first1=Praveen |last2=Trusko |first2=Brett E. |title=Global Innovation Science Handbook |date=5 February 2014 |publisher=McGraw Hill Professional |isbn=978-0-07-179271-4 |pages=389 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rhmwAgAAQBAJ&q=Nine+windows+multiscreen |access-date=3 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Tague |first1=Nancy R. |title=The Quality Toolbox |date=31 December 2023 |publisher=Quality Press |isbn=978-1-63694-123-3 |pages=381–384 |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0hLqEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22nine+windows%22+%22ASQ%22&pg=PA382 |access-date=3 July 2024 |language=en |chapter=The Tools, Section 3}}</ref>

The approach is based on the [[Theory of Inventive Problem Solving]] (TRIZ) and involves creating a {{nobr|3 × 3}} matrix and placing the current problem in the center.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=what is the Nine Windows technique? |url=https://asq.org/quality-resources/nine-windows |publisher=American Society for Quality |access-date=3 July 2024}}</ref> 

{| class="wikitable"
|+ Nine-windows matrix
!  !! Past !! Present !! Future
|-
! Super-system
|  ||  || 
|-
! System
|  || Current issue || 
|-
! Sub-system
|  ||  || 
|}


The 3 × 3 matrix is divided into three problem-solving levels:<ref name=":0" /> 
* '''Super-system''', also known as the macro system, refers to the external components and environment that currently interact with the problem or system.
* '''System''' refers to the problem or system itself.
* '''Sub-system''', also known as the micro system, refers to the parts or components of the problem or system.
